claim: In the three-dimensional model of active Brownian spheres carrying a point dipole along their propulsion direction (Kelidou et al.), at volume fraction 0.010 the system stays an active gas of mostly unbound particles for dipolar coupling lambda below 6; above 6, an active force beyond a threshold that rises with lambda breaks the aggregates back into a gas -- at lambda = 6.25 the chains are mostly destroyed already at f_a = 20.

numbers.name: dipolar_coupling_strength
numbers.note: the coupling below which no significant structure forms at this density.

numbers.note: the coupling of the example below.

numbers.name: reduced_active_force
numbers.note: the active force at which chains are mostly destroyed at lambda = 6.25.

validity_conditions: A MODEL RESULT. Three-dimensional overdamped active Brownian spheres with a WCA core and a point magnetic dipole along the propulsion direction, no hydrodynamics; lambda = mu^2/(kT sigma^3), f_a = Fa sigma/kT, gamma_t* = 3 so that the Peclet number va = f_a/3; HOOMD-blue on GPU (version not stated), time step 2e-4 tau with tau = 1/Dr, 8,788 particles, dipole sum without Ewald (see dipolar_active_brownian_spheres_dipole_sum_without_ewald_at_low_density); steady state reached from equilibrated passive systems by raising the active force gradually; states by cluster analysis with a 1.2 sigma neighbour cutoff: gas below half the particles polymerised, string fluid above half with the largest cluster under 70%, percolated network at 70% or more. Three-dimensional volume fraction pi rho*/6: 0.010 at rho* = 0.02 and 0.08 at rho* = 0.15. Reduced density rho* = 0.02. The threshold line is figure-only; the authors estimate it as the active force equal to the head-to-tail dipole force at the nearest-neighbour distance.
